title: Tangents and normals

points.text: Equation of the tangent at a given point
Equation of the normal at a given point

bigPicture: The tangent touches the curve with the same gradient; the normal is perpendicular to it at the same point.

keyTerms.def: line with the curve's gradient at the point

workedExamples.title: Normal
workedExamples.prompt: Find the normal to y = x² − 3x at x = 2.

practice.prompt: Find the tangent to y = x³ − 2x + 1 at (1, 0) and where it meets the curve again.
Find the equation of the normal to y = e^x + x at x = 0.5 (use the GDC for the gradient).

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: Why must the normal's gradient multiply with the tangent's to give −1?
